tutorials.title: Install Windows 11 from a USB flash drive
steps: Back up your files. A clean install erases the drive you install on.
On another working PC, download the Windows 11 Media Creation Tool from microsoft.com.
Plug in a USB drive of 8 GB or more and use the tool to create the installation USB.
Plug the USB into the target PC, restart, and press the boot menu key (often F12, F2, Esc or Del).
Choose the USB drive, pick your language, and click Install now.
Select Custom install, choose the drive or partition, and click Next.
Wait for the restarts, then set up your region, account and privacy options.
Open Windows Update and install drivers and updates.

tutorials.title: Dual-boot Kali Linux with Windows
steps: Back up your important files first. Changing partitions always carries some risk.
In Windows, open Disk Management, right-click your main drive and choose Shrink Volume to free at least 40 GB.
Turn off Fast Startup in Windows power options so the drive is released properly.
Download the Kali Linux installer ISO from kali.org and write it to a USB drive using Rufus or balenaEtcher.
Restart, open the boot menu, and boot from the USB drive.
Choose Graphical install and follow the language and network steps.
At partitioning, choose Manual and install only into the free space you created.
Finish the install, restart, and pick Kali or Windows from the boot menu.
